# The subgroups generated by families of almost-simple factors

Author: Worker 161 (Task 6631, with Worker 162).

This module is an internal step toward the proof of
[`SimpleFactorDecompositionStatement`](SimpleFactorDecompositionStatement.md), Conrad's
decomposition theorem for semisimple groups (*Reductive group schemes*, Theorem 5.1.19,
p.150). For an almost-simple cover `D : AlmostSimpleCover G` of a semisimple group
(see [`SimpleFactorCover`](SimpleFactorCover.md)) and a set `s` of indices, it constructs
Conrad's subgroup `G_s` as the image of the subproduct of the factors indexed by `s`, and
proves clauses 5–8 of the statement for it. All declarations are in the namespace
`Langlands.GroupScheme.SimpleFactor`. Throughout, `k : Type u` is a field, group schemes
are over `Spec k`, and "range", "normal", `≤` and `⊥` refer to `SubgroupFunctor.range`,
`SubgroupFunctor.IsNormal` and the order on subgroup functors, tested on every test
scheme.

## Subproducts

- Two private instances: smooth geometrically connected morphisms are stable under
  composition and contain identities, as needed by the published `prop_pi_hom`.
- `D.subproduct s` is `pi (fun i : s => D.factor i)`.
- `D.subproduct_geometry s`: the structure morphism of the subproduct is smooth,
  geometrically connected and affine. Proof: each factor is connected reductive, hence
  smooth, affine and (over a field) geometrically connected (published
  `geometricallyConnected_of_connected`); the published `prop_pi_hom` transfers these
  properties to finite products. The proof needs
  `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false`.

## Images of subproducts

`D.IsSubfamilyImage s b fac`, for `b : B ⟶ G` and `fac : D.subproduct s ⟶ B`, records that

- `b` is `IsClosedSubgroup`;
- `fac ≫ b = piSubsetInclusionHom D.factor s ≫ D.mul` (the subproduct inclusion followed by
  the multiplication);
- `fac` is quasi-compact, flat and surjective;
- `B` is smooth and connected.

`D.exists_isSubfamilyImage hG s`: for semisimple `G`, such `B`, `b`, `fac` exist. This is
the published `HomImage.exists_image` (image of a homomorphism from a smooth connected
affine group to an affine group locally of finite type, over a field) applied to
`piSubsetInclusionHom D.factor s ≫ D.mul`.

For `h : D.IsSubfamilyImage s b fac`:

- `h.mono`: `b` is a monomorphism.
- `h.isNormal_range`: `range b` is normal in `G`. Proof: the subproduct is normal in the
  product (published `isNormal_range_piSubsetInclusionHom`), and its image under the flat
  surjection `D.mul` is normal (`isNormal_range_of_image`).
- `h.isNormalSmooth` (clause 5, first part) and `h.isSemisimple hG`: `B` is semisimple, by
  the published `IsSemisimple.of_normalSubgroup` (clause 5, second part).
- `h.factor_comp i`: the `i`-th factor of the subproduct followed by `fac` and `b` is
  `D.inclusion i`.
- `h.range_inclusion_le hi` (clause 6, first part): for `i ∈ s`, the range of
  `D.inclusion i` lies in `range b`.
- `h.range_le_of_isClosedSubgroup hn hle` (clause 6, second part): if a closed subgroup
  `n : K ⟶ G` contains the factors indexed by `s`, then `range b ≤ range n`. Proof: the
  range of `piSubsetInclusionHom D.factor s ≫ D.mul` lies in `range n`
  (`range_piSubsetInclusionHom_comp_le_iff`), and this descends along the flat surjection
  `fac` (`range_le_of_comp_le`).
- `h.range_le_commutant F hle`: similarly, if the selected factors lie in `commutant F`,
  so does `range b`.
- `h.mem_iff hG i`: `i ∈ s` if and only if the range of `D.inclusion i` lies in `range b`.
  If `i ∉ s`, all selected factors commute with factor `i`, so `range b` lies in its
  commutant, and factor `i` would lie in its own commutant.
- `h.subcover`: the selected factors, with `mul := fac`, form an `AlmostSimpleCover B`.
  Each factor map into `B` is a closed immersion because its composite with the closed
  immersion `b` is `D.inclusion i` (published `IsClosedSubgroup.of_comp`).
  `h.subcover_inclusion_comp j` records `h.subcover.inclusion j ≫ b = D.inclusion j`.
- `h.exists_isMinimalNormalSmooth hG hi` (clause 7, first part): for `i ∈ s` there is
  `c : D.factor i ⟶ B` with `c ≫ b = D.inclusion i` and `IsMinimalNormalSmooth c` in `B`.
  This is `isMinimalNormalSmooth_inclusion` for the subcover, using that `B` is semisimple.
- `h.exists_range_eq_of_isMinimalNormalSmooth hG n hn` (clause 7, second part): every
  minimal `n : K ⟶ B` has `range (n ≫ b) = range (D.inclusion i)` for some `i ∈ s`, by
  `exists_range_eq_inclusion` for the subcover.
- `h.support_eq hG hn`: if `range n = range b`, then `D.support n = s` (by `mem_iff`).
- `h.range_eq_of_support hG hn hs` (clause 8, existence): if `IsNormalSmooth n` and
  `s = D.support n`, then `range n = range b`.

## Proof of `range_eq_of_support`

The inclusion `range b ≤ range n` is `range_le_of_isClosedSubgroup`, since `n` contains the
factors in its support. For the reverse inclusion, `K` is semisimple
(`IsSemisimple.of_normalSubgroup`), hence perfect: `derivedSubgroup K = ⊤` by the published
`semisimplePerfect`. By `range_le_of_derivedSubgroup_eq_top` it suffices to show that the
image `[x, y] ≫ n` of every commutator of points `x, y` of `K` lies in `range b`; by fppf
descent of membership (published `SubgroupFunctor.mem_range_of_comp_mem_range`) this may
be checked after a quasi-compact, flat, surjective refinement. After refining twice
(`exists_refinement_lift`, `effectiveEpi_comp_left`), `x ≫ n` and `y ≫ n` become images of
points of the product under `D.mul`, and each splits (`exists_mul_mem_range_piSubset`) as
`a * c` with `a` in the image `G_s` of the subproduct on `s` and `c` in the image of the
subproduct on the complement `sᶜ`. The factors outside `s` lie in
`commutant (range n)` (`range_le_commutant_of_notMem_support`) and commute with the factors
in `s`, so `c₁` commutes with `a₂ * c₂ ∈ range n` and `c₂` commutes with `a₁`. Then
`commutator_mul_mul_eq` gives `[a₁ c₁, a₂ c₂] = [a₁, a₂]`, which lies in the image of the
subproduct on `s`, hence in `range b`.

## Provenance

The construction of `G_s` as an image and all proofs are internal to this formalization.
Conrad defines `G_J` as the subgroup generated by the `G_i` with `i ∈ J`; clause 6 of the
statement characterizes it as the smallest closed subgroup containing them, which is what
`range_inclusion_le` and `range_le_of_isClosedSubgroup` prove. Conrad derives the
remaining properties from the split case and Galois descent (pp.150–151); the
perfectness argument above works directly over `k`.
